docs.title: Fusion Manage Add-in for Fusion
docs.text:
Publish your released designs from Fusion into Fusion Manage as manufacturing items, bills of materials (BOMs) and files. Engineering keeps designing in Fusion. Manufacturing gets a controlled record in Fusion Manage. Nothing crosses until you choose to publish.

Install the add-in See how it works

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: What you'll do here: set up the Item Workspace and Export tabs of Preferences: which Fusion Manage workspace the add-in writes to, which design property fills which field, and where exported files are attached. Do it once, before the first publish. The Connection tab is covered in Installation and Authentication.

docs.title: Quick steps
docs.text:
1. Sign in and connect to your tenant.
  2. Open Manage ▸ Item Management ▸ Administration ▸ Preferences ▸ Item Workspace.
  3. Choose your Items workspace and wait for the tick.
  4. Click Add default fields, and check the rows that appear (up to nine, one for each field your workspace has) (Default fields).
  5. Click Save.

If a picklist field is mapped, its values must match in both systems (Picklists). Unfamiliar words are in the Glossary.

docs.title: In this page
docs.text:
Section Read it when Item Workspace You are choosing the workspace, mapping fields, setting default values or linking components. Export destinations You want STEP, PDF, DWG or DXF files to attach to an item or a component.

To know what the add-in reads from your design, and what must be true of it first, see Manufacturing Data Model.

docs.title: Item Workspace
docs.text:
This section covers the Item Workspace tab of Preferences: which Fusion Manage workspace the add-in writes to, and how each property it reads from the Manufacturing Data Model is mapped to a field there. The mapping of properties to fields is described under Field mapping.

You normally set it up once, then share it with colleagues through the hub (Save to Fusion Hub).

docs.title: The Items workspace
docs.text:
The add-in currently works with one workspace kind, Items ("Manufacturing items created in Fusion Manage"). On the Item Workspace tab you will find a card for it with the parts below. The numbers in the screenshot match the table.

# Part What it does 1 Workspace A drop-down of the Revision Controlled Workspace type in your tenant, and no other type. Choose the one that holds your items by name (Which workspaces are listed). 2 Validation Happens automatically when you pick a workspace or open the tab. It checks the workspace and loads its field list so the pickers below can show real field names. The mapping controls stay disabled until the workspace validates (a tick appears next to the workspace). 3 Component linking Optional, see Component linking. 4 Field mapping Which Data Model property fills which Fusion Manage field. Each row pairs one with the other (Field mapping). 5 Add default fields At the top right of the Field mapping section. It fills the list with the standard nine mappings instead of you adding them one at a time. It is the quickest start, and it replaces the rows already there (Default fields). 6 Default Fusion Manage Values Fields set to a fixed value on every published item (Default Fusion Manage Values).

Click Save when you are done. Saving is refused while the settings have problems, and the message says what to fix.

docs.title: Which workspaces are listed
docs.text:
The Workspace drop-down does not list every workspace in your tenant. It lists only workspaces whose workspace type in Fusion Manage is Revision Controlled Workspace, under the heading "Revision Controlled Workspaces". Items in a workspace of this type have revisions and a lifecycle, which is what the add-in publishes to.

Some workspaces are left out on purpose:

  • Workspaces of any other workspace type.
  • Workspaces that Fusion Manage marks as controlled, such as Components and Drawings, which do not hold the items you publish.
  • Deleted workspaces.

If your Items workspace is missing from the list, its type is the usual reason. The drop-down then says "No revision controlled workspaces found" if there are none at all, or shows the reason the list could not be read. Ask your Fusion Manage administrator to check the type of the workspace.

docs.title: Field mapping
docs.text:
Each row of Mapped fields pairs a Fusion Manage item field (left) with the component property that fills it (right):

Column Meaning Fusion Manage Item Field The Fusion Manage field it fills, shown with its title and ID. Component Property The source: a Data Model property.

docs.title: Available sources
docs.text:
• Built-in fields: Item Number, Part number, Name, Description, Revision, Material, Lifecycle state and Thumbnail. Item Number is the one that matters most: see The item number.
  • Custom and base properties: any property defined on your Manufacturing Data Model items can be mapped by name.
  • Physical properties: Mass, Volume, Area, Density, Length, Width and Height (Length, Width and Height are the bounding box). They are read only when a mapping uses them.

docs.title: The item number
docs.text:
The item number is the key to everything

The add-in decides whether to create or update an item by looking for its item number in your Items workspace. Two things must be true:

  1. In the add-in: Item Number is mapped to the Fusion Manage field that holds it, usually NUMBER. Add default fields does this for you.
  2. In Fusion Manage: that field is part of the item descriptor of the Items workspace. The add-in finds items by searching their descriptor, so an item whose descriptor does not include the number cannot be found (How the search matches).
Component property        Fusion Manage item field
Item Number         =     Number (NUMBER)

Item Number is not Part number

Part number is a separate component property that you can map to any field you like, but it is never used to match items. The add-in uses it only to find the component you selected in the open design (Manufacturing Data Model). Matching always uses Item Number.

How the item number is used:

Rule What it means If it is not met Item Number must be mapped One row with the component property Item Number and the Fusion Manage field that holds the item number (usually NUMBER). Saving is refused: Item Number is not mapped. Add a mapped field with the Component Property 'Item Number' and the Fusion Manage Item Field 'NUMBER'. The workspace is reported as not set up, and the ribbon buttons stay greyed out. The number must be in the descriptor In Fusion Manage, the Items workspace's item descriptor must include the item number field (NUMBER), at the start. Titles and other fields may follow, set off by -. This is set in Fusion Manage, not in the add-in, and the add-in cannot check it. Existing items are not found and show as New. It is mapped once A component property can be mapped once, and a Fusion Manage field filled once. The settings report the duplicate and will not save. Items are found by it At publish, the add-in searches the Items workspace for the component's item number, against each item's descriptor (below). Nothing else is used to match. See the outcomes below. A component needs one A component with no item number cannot be published or opened in the Item Panel. It is Skipped, and so is everything below it in the BOM.

docs.title: How the search matches
docs.text:
Fusion Manage identifies each item by its descriptor, the name it shows for the item, which each workspace builds from its fields. The add-in searches the descriptor for the item number. The number of an item is read as the part of its descriptor before -, compared without capitals and without spaces at the ends. So a descriptor can carry more after the number, set off by -:

Item descriptor in Fusion Manage Item number searched Matches PN-1001 PN-1001 Yes PN-1001 - Bracket PN-1001 Yes: the number is the part before - pn-1001 - Bracket PN-1001 Yes: capitals are ignored Bracket PN-1001 No: the descriptor does not start with the number

Check your workspace's descriptor

The item number field (NUMBER) must be part of the Items workspace's descriptor, at the start. A descriptor built another way, for example from the title alone, means the add-in will not find items that already exist. It shows those components as New, so a publish would try to create them again. Ask your Fusion Manage administrator to check the item descriptor of the Items workspace before your first publish.

docs.title: Rules the settings enforce
docs.text:
• A workspace must be chosen from the Workspace drop-down. You pick it by name; the add-in works out the rest.
  • Every row needs both a source and a Fusion Manage field.
  • Item Number must be mapped to the Fusion Manage field that holds it (The item number).
  • A source can be mapped only once, and a Fusion Manage field can be filled only once, whether by a mapping, a default value or the component-linking field.

docs.title: Data types: how a value is fitted to its field
docs.text:
A component property reaches the add-in as a value, and the Fusion Manage field it is mapped to has a data type. The add-in looks at the type of the target field and fits the value to it before sending. Nothing is configured for this: it follows from the field you map to.

Component property Fusion Manage field What the add-in does Text, such as Name, Description or a custom text property Text field Sent as it is. A picklist value, such as a single select custom property (Type) Picklist field Finds the picklist option with the same text and sends a link to that option (Picklists). A number, such as a custom number property Number field Rounded to the decimal places the field takes (Numbers). A physical property: Mass, Volume, Area, Density, Length, Width or Height Number field, usually with a unit Converted to the unit the field is set to, then rounded and sent as a plain number (Physical properties). Thumbnail Image field Sent as an image file (Thumbnail). Any other value Any other field Sent as text, with no conversion.

docs.title: Picklists
docs.text:
A picklist field in Fusion Manage does not accept text. It takes a link to one of its options. So when the target is a picklist, the add-in reads the field's options and looks for the one whose title matches the value, ignoring capitals and spaces at either end.

Value from Fusion Options in Fusion Manage Result Top Level Assembly Top Level Assembly, Part Sent: the matching option top level assembly Top Level Assembly, Part Sent: capitals and end spaces are ignored Assembly Top Level Assembly, Part Not sent: there is no such option

A value with no matching option is left out, because Fusion Manage would refuse the whole item for it. The item is still published without that field, and the run's files record: 'Assembly' is not an option of TYPE in Fusion Manage, so it was not sent. See Troubleshooting and Limitations.

This is why a picklist in Fusion (a single select custom property) and the picklist in Fusion Manage it is mapped to must hold the same values. The same applies to a default value set on a picklist field, where you choose from the field's own options.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
A number field refuses more decimal digits than its precision (the number of decimal places set on the field in Fusion Manage). The add-in rounds the value to that many places (halves round up) before sending it.

Value from Fusion Field precision Sent 0.104455 3 decimal places 0.104 12.5 0 decimal places 13 12.5 no limit set 12.5

The same rounding is used when comparing. A Fusion value of 0.104455 against 0.104 already in Fusion Manage is shown as a match, not a change, so rounding alone never causes an update.

docs.title: Physical properties and units
docs.text:
The Data Model gives a physical property in Fusion's own units: centimetres for lengths, areas and volumes, and kilograms for mass. A Fusion Manage number field can be set to a unit of its own, for example millimetres. When it is, the add-in converts the value to that unit before rounding and sending it.

Fusion gives Field is set to Sent 10 cm (Length) millimetres 100 2.5 kg (Mass) grams 2500 0.5 kg (Mass) pounds 1.1 (rounded to the field's precision)
  • Conversion covers length (mm, cm, m, in, ft), mass (mg, g, kg, oz, lb) and their square, cubic and per-volume forms (area, volume, density). It only converts between units of the same kind.
  • If the field states no unit, or its unit is one the add-in does not know, or it measures something different, the value is sent unchanged and a warning is logged.
  • Only the number is sent, with no unit, because a Fusion Manage number field refuses text such as 10 mm.

Set the unit on the field

To receive a value in millimetres, set the field's unit to millimetres in Fusion Manage. The add-in converts to whatever the field says, so a field with no unit receives Fusion's own centimetres and kilograms as they are.

docs.title: Thumbnail
docs.text: An image field takes a file, not text. The add-in fetches a fresh thumbnail when it publishes the item and sends it as an image. An image cannot be compared with what is already there, so it is sent on every publish: with a create, and with an update even when nothing else differs. An item with a mapped thumbnail is therefore updated by every publish.

docs.title: Default fields
docs.text:
Add default fields loads the standard set of mappings in one click, so you do not build them row by row. It is the fastest way to set up a workspace that follows the out-of-the-box layout.

To use it:

  1. Choose your Items workspace and wait for the tick. The button needs the workspace to be validated, so it knows which fields exist.
  2. Click Add default fields and read the Load default fields? question.
  3. Click Load default fields to go ahead, or Cancel to leave your mappings as they are.
  4. Check the Mapped fields list, adjust it if you need to, then click Save. The rows are only on screen until you save.

It replaces your mappings

Loading the defaults replaces all existing field mappings with the standard set. Any mapping you added or changed is removed. A confirmation (Load default fields?) asks first, and you can cancel. Default Fusion Manage Values and the component-linking field are not part of the defaults.

docs.title: What is added
docs.text:
# Data Model source Fusion Manage field ID Notes 1 Item Number NUMBER Required. Existing items are found by their item number 2 Name TITLE 3 Description DESCRIPTION 4 Thumbnail IMAGE The component's image, sent as a file 5 Material MATERIAL Read from the Data Model's materialName 6 Physical Height HEIGHT Bounding box 7 Physical Width WIDTH Bounding box 8 Physical Length LENGTH Bounding box 9 Physical Mass ITEM_WEIGHT Converted to the field's unit

Dimensions and mass are converted to the unit each Fusion Manage field is set to, and sent as plain numbers (Physical properties and units). Physical properties are only available once the Data Model has finished calculating them (Manufacturing Data Model).

docs.title: Which fields your workspace needs
docs.text:
Each default writes to a Fusion Manage field by its field ID. Only one of the nine is required:

Field ID Needed? Why NUMBER Required It holds the item number, which is how items are found (The item number). TITLE, DESCRIPTION, IMAGE, MATERIAL, HEIGHT, WIDTH, LENGTH, ITEM_WEIGHT Optional Each is only filled if your workspace has a field with that ID. Without it, that mapping is simply not made, and nothing else is affected.

The add-in does not depend on any other field IDs. Map the fields you want published, and leave out the rest.

Fusion Manage's own required fields

If your Items workspace marks other fields as required in Fusion Manage, a new item needs a value for each. Map them, or give them a default value. The add-in does not check this in advance: Fusion Manage refuses an item that lacks one, and the run records its reason.

Missing fields are skipped, not reported

Once the workspace has been validated, Add default fields leaves out any default whose field ID does not exist in your workspace. It does not warn you. If you load the defaults and a row you expected is missing, the field is missing, or its ID is different, in Fusion Manage.

Check the result after loading: the Mapped fields list shows a row for each default your workspace has a field for, up to nine. If your workspace has been customised, add or correct the missing rows by hand.

docs.title: Default Fusion Manage Values
docs.text: A default value sets a Fusion Manage item field to the same value on every published item, regardless of the design. Choose Add default value, pick the field, then enter or choose the value (a picklist field offers its options). For an existing item, a default value is applied when the item lacks it.

docs.title: Component linking
docs.text: If your Items workspace has a field that links an item to a record in the Fusion Manage components picklist, choose it under Component linking (Choose the linking field…). When publishing, the add-in links each item to its component: first through the link stored in the Data Model, and if there is none, by searching the component picklist for the item number. If neither finds it, the item is still published and the step is recorded as a failed "component link" in the run's files.

docs.title: When the buttons light up
docs.text: The ribbon and context-menu buttons, other than Preferences and Export, stay disabled until the Items workspace is usable: a workspace is chosen, and the mappings are valid. The tooltip says what is still missing. The Export window opens either way; it turns off only its Item destination, and says why.

docs.title: Export destinations
docs.text:
The Export tab of Preferences decides where each exported file is attached in Fusion Manage. You choose a destination for each file format, and it is the one the Export window starts on.

Format What it is Made from STEP A 3D model The open design PDF To print or share The open drawing DWG For AutoCAD The open drawing DXF For CAM and laser cutting The open drawing

Each format has two choices:

Destination The file is attached to In the workspace Item The item of the component Items Component The component record Components

Every format starts on Item. Click Save after changing one.

docs.title: How the Export window uses it
docs.text:
The Export window starts on the destination you set here for the format you pick. You can still choose the other one for a single export, and the setting is not changed.

The window starts on the other destination instead when the one you set cannot be used:

  • The Items workspace is not set up, so Item is off. The window says so.
  • The connection is incomplete, so Component is off. The window says so, and asks you to complete it in Preferences.
  • You may not attach files there. Attaching needs View Items, Add Attachments and Edit Attachments in that workspace (Permissions in Fusion Manage).
  • No workspace called Components is found in Fusion Manage, so Component is off.

The window opens either way, and turns off only the destination that cannot be used, with its reason. For how to export, see The Export Window.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Plain-English meanings of the terms used in this documentation. Terms are in alphabetical order.

Term Meaning APS (Autodesk Platform Services) Autodesk's developer platform. The add-in uses it to sign you in and to read design data. You need an APS application to get a Client ID. Bill of materials (BOM) The list of parts that make up an assembly, with how many of each. The add-in compares the design's BOM with the one in Fusion Manage. Callback URL The local address your browser returns to after you sign in. It is http://localhost:8765/callback unless you change the port. Client ID A code that identifies the add-in to Autodesk when you sign in. You get it from your APS application. It is not a password. Component A part or assembly in a Fusion design. Component linking An optional setting that links a Fusion Manage item to a record in the Fusion Manage components list. Details Panel The panel beside the BOM in the Publish panel. It shows what publishing will change for the selected component. Field mapping The rule that says which design property fills which Fusion Manage field. For example, Description fills DESCRIPTION. Fusion Manage Autodesk's cloud product lifecycle management (PLM) system. It holds the manufactured items. Hub Your organisation's workspace in Autodesk. Settings are kept per hub. Item A record in Fusion Manage for a manufactured part, with its own BOM, files and release workflow. Item number The number Fusion Manage finds an item by. It is the component's Item Number in the Manufacturing Data Model, and it is what the add-in matches on. A component with no item number cannot be published. Job One publish. The Job Queue lists jobs that are waiting, running and finished. Manufacturing Data Model (MDM) The description of your design that Fusion saves in the cloud: components, properties, BOM structure and thumbnails. The add-in reads it and never changes it. Part number What Fusion calls a component. The add-in uses it only to find the component you selected in the open design, then reads that component's item number from the Manufacturing Data Model. Fusion Manage is not searched by it. Publish Create or update items and BOMs in Fusion Manage from a design. Only the differences are sent. Representation A file that describes an item, such as a STEP file or a drawing PDF. You upload these yourself. They are never sent by a publish. Tenant Your company's Fusion Manage site. It is the part before .autodeskplm360.net in your Fusion Manage address. Where used The assemblies that contain a given item. Workflow The approval steps an item goes through in Fusion Manage, for example to release it. Workspace A section of Fusion Manage that holds one kind of record. This add-in works with the Items workspace.

docs.title: Installation and Authentication
docs.text: What you'll do here: install the add-in in Fusion and sign in to Fusion Manage. Install it first, then choose your route: Admin Route for the Hub Admin who sets it up, Member Route for everyone else.

docs.title: 1. Install the add-in
docs.text:
1. Download the latest zip from the Releases page and unzip it. You get a folder named Fusion Manage Item Management, which holds Fusion Manage Item Management.py and Fusion Manage Item Management.manifest.
  2. In Fusion open Utilities ▸ Add-Ins ▸ Scripts and Add-Ins, switch to the Add-Ins tab, click + (add existing add-in) and browse to the folder.
  3. Select Fusion Manage Item Management in the list and click Run. Tick Run on Startup if you want it to load with Fusion.

The add-in supports Windows and macOS. Once it is running, an Export panel and an Item Management panel appear in the Manage tab of the Design and Drawing workspaces. Most buttons stay greyed out until setup is complete.

docs.title: Choose your route
docs.text:
Admin Route Member Route

Admin Route is for the Hub Admin who sets the add-in up for the hub, once. Member Route is for everyone else in the hub, once a Hub Admin has published the setup.

Has another Hub Admin already set this up?

Then do the Member Route, even if you are a Hub Admin yourself. The hub only needs one setup, and the Configuration File already holds it, so you do not need your own APS app or tenant. If the setup wizard opens, choose Already set up, then click Find Configuration File and pick the file. You can still change the settings afterwards as a Hub Admin, and publish them again with Save & Publish.

docs.title: 2. Get a Client ID
docs.text:
Admin Route. Members skip to the Member Route.

The add-in signs in through Autodesk Platform Services (APS), so it needs an APS application. The application's Client ID identifies the add-in when you sign in. This is done on the APS website, not in Fusion.

You may already have one

If your organisation has already created an application for this add-in, ask for its Client ID and skip to stage 3. One application can be shared by everyone; each person still signs in with their own Autodesk account.

What you need first:

  • An Autodesk account that can sign in at aps.autodesk.com.
  • An APS subscription (Free or Paid tier) assigned to a team.
  • A Team Administrator to set up the APS Developer Hub, if your organisation does not have one yet. See Administrator setup.

docs.title: 2.1 Create the application
docs.text:
1. Sign in at aps.autodesk.com and open My Applications.
  2. Click Create application.

  3. When asked for the application type, choose Desktop, Mobile, Single-Page App.

    Choose this type

    The add-in signs in with PKCE and never holds a client secret. This is the type APS recommends for applications that cannot protect their credentials. Do not choose Traditional Web App or Server-to-Server App.

  4. Enter an application name and description, for example Fusion Manage Add-in.

  5. Select the APIs the add-in uses: the Manufacturing Data Model API (to read designs) and the Identity API (for your profile picture). Select the matching entries your portal offers.

  6. Set the Callback URL to exactly:

    http://localhost:8765/callback

    If you will use a different callback port in the add-in, use that port here instead. The two must match exactly.

  7. Save the application.

Labels can change

The APS portal is updated from time to time, so button names and field order may differ slightly from this list. The application type, the APIs and the callback URL are what matter.

docs.title: 2.2 Copy the Client ID
docs.text:
Open the application under My Applications. Its details page shows the Client ID, a 32-character string. Copy it. You will paste it into the add-in in the next stage.

An application of this type has no client secret that you need. Never type one into the add-in.

docs.title: Administrator setup
docs.text:
Team Administrators only: APS subscription and Developer Hub

A1. Get an APS subscription (Team Administrator)

Skip this if your organisation already has an APS offering assigned to a team.

  1. Go to aps.autodesk.com and sign in or sign up. Click View options.
  2. On the APS overview page, use the Site Selector (top right) to choose your country before signing in.
  3. Click Pricing in the left-hand menu, then Add to Cart under the offering you want, then Checkout and complete the customer details.
    • A Free plan is not charged, but checkout still asks for a payment method.
    • A Paid plan needs a valid payment method.
  4. Click Access Account, which opens the Autodesk Account portal.
  5. If you administer more than one team, go to Billing and Orders ▸ Subscriptions and Contracts and confirm the APS offering is assigned to the right team.

Note

If your region is not offered in the Autodesk Store, contact aps.orders@autodesk.com.

A2. Create the APS Developer Hub (Team Administrator)

The Developer Hub is where your organisation's APS applications live, and where you control who can create them.

  1. Open manage.autodesk.com.
  2. Go to Products and Services ▸ Hubs.
  3. Choose the team the APS offering is assigned to.
  4. Click Create Hub and select APS Developer Hub.
  5. Enter a Hub Name and click Create & Activate.
  6. Under Cloud Product, click the APS Developer Hub link. This opens aps.autodesk.com/hubs.

No “APS Developer Hub” option?

The team has no APS offering assigned to it. Complete step A1 first.

A3. Add developers to the hub (Team Administrator)

  1. In the hub, open Roles and Access.
  2. Click Add Member and enter the person's email address.
  3. Choose an access level, Admin or Developer, and click Add.

Anyone who needs to create the application must be a member of the hub.

A4. Moving an existing application into the hub

If you already created the application before your organisation had a Developer Hub, move it in:

  1. Sign in at aps.autodesk.com and open My Applications.
  2. Select the application.
  3. Click Move apps to Developer Hub.
  4. Select the hub name and click Next.

You must already be a member of the hub (see A3).

More reading

This section follows Autodesk's own guide, APS Developer Hub Setup and App Migration, and the post New application types. Refer to them if your portal looks different.

docs.title: 3. Configure the connection
docs.text:
Admin Route.

Open Manage ▸ Item Management ▸ Administration ▸ Preferences. Until a Client ID is saved, the panel shows a setup wizard instead of the sign-in card. It walks you through the connection in two parts: the app and Client ID, then your tenant.

docs.title: 3.1 Set up Fusion Manage
docs.text:
The first screen, Set up Fusion Manage, asks how to start:

  • New setup shows the four steps below. Use it when nobody has set this hub up yet.
  • Already set up is for a hub another Hub Admin has already set up and published. Click Find Configuration File and choose the file (Member Route). You skip the steps below and the tenant step.

The steps for a new setup:

  1. Create an APS app. If you have not done so, follow stage 2. The wizard lists the settings the app needs: Desktop, Mobile, Single-Page Web App, grant type Authorization Code with PKCE, and the Manufacturing Data Model API and Identity API. Open the setup guide opens Autodesk's guide to creating an app.

  2. Add the callback URL. On your app's page in the APS portal, add the callback URL the wizard shows and save the app. Copy puts it on your clipboard. With the default port it is:

    http://localhost:8765/callback

  3. Enter the Client ID. Paste the Client ID from step 2.2.

  4. Sign in. Click Save and sign in. The button stays disabled until a Client ID is entered. It saves the Client ID and opens the Autodesk sign-in in your browser. Approve access there and return to Fusion (how sign-in works).

docs.title: 3.2 Connect your tenant
docs.text:
Once you are signed in, a Hub Admin sees Connect your Tenant. It is required, and the tabs stay hidden until a tenant is saved.

Click Find to fill in the tenant automatically

Open a design linked to a Fusion Manage item, then click Find. The add-in reads the tenant from that item's address and fills in the field, so you do not have to type it.

Find only works when:

  • You are signed in, because it reads the design through your Autodesk account.
  • A design is open in Fusion and is the active document. A drawing, or a document with no design, gives nothing to read.
  • The design is saved to your hub, so the Manufacturing Data Model knows it.
  • The design is linked to a Fusion Manage item. If it is not, the panel says so; open one that is, or enter the tenant yourself.

It reads only the open design, and gives up if there is no answer after a minute.

Or enter the Tenant yourself:

  1. Open Fusion Manage in your browser and look at the address bar. It looks like this:

    https://acme.autodeskplm360.net/plm/...

  2. Copy only the first part of the host name, the bit before .autodeskplm360.net. Here that is acme. Do not copy https://, .autodeskplm360.net or anything after it.

  3. Paste it into the Tenant field, so the field holds just acme.

The tenant can only be letters, digits and hyphens, never a whole address. The hub's name is not the tenant, so the add-in does not guess it.

Whichever way you filled it in, click Save and finish to keep it. Find only fills in the field; it does not save.

Anyone who is not a Hub Admin does not see this step. They are asked to find the hub's Configuration File instead (below).

docs.title: 3.3 Change the connection later
docs.text:
After setup, the same settings are on the Connection tab of Preferences.

Only a Hub Admin can change them

Settings belong to the Fusion hub that is active. When Preferences opens, the add-in checks your role in that hub, and checks again when you return to the panel. A Hub Admin can edit the Connection tab. Anyone else sees the fields greyed out, with the note "These settings come from the hub's Configuration File. Only a Hub Admin can change them." If the add-in cannot check your role, the tab is left usable, so a failed check does not lock out an admin.

To change a setting, as a Hub Admin:

  1. Open Preferences and go to the Connection tab.
  2. Edit the field. If you change the Callback port, the callback URL shown under it updates as you type.
  3. Click Save to keep the change on this computer, or Save & Publish to also share it with the hub, so your colleagues get the change (how it works). The settings are checked first, and a problem is shown instead of saving. A Save successful window confirms a save.

Two changes need a follow-up:

  • Client ID: sign-in is kept per Client ID, so after changing it you sign in again with the new one.
  • Callback port: the callback URL on your APS app must match the new port, or sign-in fails.
Setting What it is Client ID The Client ID from step 2.2. Callback port The port in your callback URL. Default 8765; allowed range 1024–65535. If you change it, change the callback URL on your APS app to match. Scopes Leave as data:read data:write data:search user-profile:read. Tenant The tenant from step 3.2.

The tab shows the callback URL it will use. It must be registered on your APS application exactly as shown. A Client ID, a valid port and at least one scope are required before you can sign in.

docs.title: Save to Fusion Hub
docs.text:
Save puts the settings on your own computer only. Save & Publish saves them and also stores them in the hub, as a Configuration File, so the other people in the hub can use the same setup without entering it themselves. Only a Hub Admin sees Save & Publish.

  1. Click Save & Publish. Once the settings pass validation and are saved on this computer, a Save to Fusion Hub window opens, showing the hub's projects and folders.
  2. Open a project, then a folder in it, where the hub's members can read files. New project (at the top of the hub) and New folder (inside a project) make one if you need it. A project of its own is best (see below).
  3. Click Save here. The add-in uploads Fusion-Manage-Item-Management-config.json to that folder and tells you which folder it went to.

docs.title: Give your members access to the file
docs.text:
It is recommended to create a new project for the Configuration File, with New project, and save it there. A project of its own keeps the file out of the way of design data, and lets you control who can see it in one place. Saving the file does not give anyone access to it. Members can only find it, read it and download it if they have access, so set that up once, straight after the first Save & Publish:

  1. In Fusion, open the project (or the folder) the file is in, and go to its Members and Permissions tab.
  2. Make sure everyone who needs the add-in is there with Reader access. Reader is enough to view and download the file, and members never need to change it. Use Add member to add people by email, or a group to add several at once. A group that already holds your members, such as Everyone (System Group), is the quickest way, if it suits who may see the file.
  3. Check the Permission level of each person or group. Anyone not listed, or with no access, will not see the file when they look for it.

Keep editing for Hub Admins

Only the Hub Admins who publish need to be able to add files to the folder. Everyone else can be a Reader.

What to know:

  • It holds your setup, not anyone's sign-in. The file has the tenant, workspaces, field mappings, exports, and the Client ID with its callback port and scopes, so members can sign in without making an APS app. It never holds sign-in tokens or a client secret.
  • The upload uses your Fusion session. It needs no extra permission, but you must be allowed to add files to the folder you pick. If not, the add-in says so.
  • It is for the active hub. A file saved from one hub is refused by another.
  • Publish again after a change. Each Save & Publish uploads the file again to the folder you choose. Choose the folder your colleagues already use, so they keep reading the same file.
  • Members find it once. After that, their add-in reads it again each time Preferences opens, so a change you publish reaches them without them doing anything (what members do).

docs.title: Members: connect with the hub's Configuration File
docs.text:
Member Route.

Each Fusion hub has its own settings, so switching hubs in Fusion switches the settings too. Only a Hub Admin of the hub can change them. When you open Preferences the add-in checks your role in the active hub. If you are a member, not a Hub Admin, you do not create an APS app, copy a Client ID or enter a tenant. A Hub Admin has done that once and published the result, and you use it.

Before you start: a Hub Admin must have used Save & Publish (above) so the file is in the hub, and given you Reader access to the project it is in (how). If you cannot find the file, ask a Hub Admin where it is and whether you have access.

docs.title: The route
docs.text:
1. Install the add-in. Follow stage 1. It is the same for everyone.
  2. Make the right hub active. In Fusion, open the hub the setup was published for. A file from another hub is refused.
  3. Open Preferences. Choose Manage ▸ Item Management ▸ Administration ▸ Preferences. The panel shows Find your Configuration File, with the hub's name. Click Find Configuration File.

  4. Open the folder. The Find the Configuration File window lists the hub's projects. Open the project and folders the Hub Admin saved the file in. Use this file stays greyed out until you choose a file.

  5. Choose the file. Click Fusion-Manage-Item-Management-config.json. The window names it at the bottom (Selected …). Click Use this file.

  6. Sign in. The add-in reads the file and the panel changes to Sign in to Fusion Manage, with the hub's name. Click Sign in, approve access in your browser and return to Fusion. You sign in with your own Autodesk account (how sign-in works).

  7. Check the Configuration tab. Once you are signed in, the panel opens on the Configuration tab. It shows the file you are using and whether it is up to date. Your role shows as Member.

You are ready to use the add-in. There is nothing else to set up.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The file is the setup. It holds the tenant, workspaces, field mappings, exports, and the Client ID with its callback port and scopes. The add-in takes these from it, so you do not enter them. It never holds sign-in tokens, so you still sign in yourself.
  • Your settings are read-only. The Connection, Item Workspace and Export tabs show what the file defines, with fields greyed out and the note "These settings come from the hub's Configuration File. Only a Hub Admin can change them." Members do not see Save & Publish.

  • It stays up to date. The file is read again each time Preferences opens, so a change a Hub Admin publishes reaches you without you doing anything. The status at the top of the Configuration tab says where you stand:

    Status Meaning Up to date You are using the latest file in the hub. It shows when it was read or checked. Checking for updates… The add-in is asking the hub if the file has changed. Updated to the latest version The file had changed, and you now use the new one. It names who changed it. Could not check for updates The check got no answer. The add-in keeps the file you have, so try again in a moment.

  • Check for updates asks the hub at once, without closing Preferences. Change file lets you pick a different file, for example if the Hub Admin moved it to another folder.

  • The file's details. The card shows the file's name and project, Last updated in the hub, Updated by, its Version in the hub, and Last read by you.
  • Your own Client ID is kept. If you already had a Client ID, the add-in keeps it, and your sign-in, and takes only the setup from the file.
  • Files that are refused: one saved from another hub, one over 1 MB, or one that is not a Fusion Manage Item Management configuration. A file with no Client ID is also refused, so ask the Hub Admin to publish again.

docs.title: How sign-in works
docs.text:
The wizard's Save and sign in button starts sign-in for you. Your browser opens the Autodesk sign-in page; sign in and approve access, and the browser shows Authorization received. Return to Fusion and the panel unlocks its tabs. Sign-in waits up to 180 seconds, and Cancel ends it sooner. Later, if you have signed out or your session has expired, Sign in on the Preferences panel does the same. To sign out, use the account menu in the panel header, which removes the stored tokens for the current Client ID.

This section explains what happens behind that. The add-in uses the OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow with PKCE. Your password is only ever entered on the Autodesk sign-in page, never in Fusion or the add-in.

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User
    participant Addin as Fusion Manage add-in
    participant Browser as Web browser
    participant APS as Autodesk sign-in (APS)
    participant Store as Secure token store
    participant Svc as Data Model and Fusion Manage

    User->>Addin: Click Sign in
    Note over Addin: Create PKCE code verifier,<br/>code challenge and state
    Addin->>Addin: Listen on 127.0.0.1 at the callback port
    Addin->>Browser: Open the authorize URL<br/>(client ID, scopes, challenge, state)
    Browser->>APS: Request sign-in
    User->>APS: Sign in and approve access
    APS-->>Browser: Redirect to localhost callback<br/>with code and state
    Browser->>Addin: GET /callback?code=...&state=...
    Note over Addin: Check state matches,<br/>otherwise reject the sign-in
    Addin-->>Browser: "Authorization received. Return to Fusion."
    Addin->>APS: Exchange code and code verifier for tokens<br/>(no client secret)
    APS-->>Addin: Access token and refresh token
    Addin->>Store: Save tokens, encrypted<br/>(Windows DPAPI or macOS Keychain)
    Addin-->>User: Panels unlock

    rect rgb(238, 242, 255)
    Note over Addin,Svc: Every later request
    Addin->>Store: Load tokens
    alt Access token still valid
        Addin->>Svc: Request with access token
    else Expires within 60 seconds
        Addin->>APS: Refresh with refresh token
        APS-->>Addin: New tokens
        Addin->>Store: Save new tokens
        Addin->>Svc: Request with new access token
    end
    end

If sign-in is cancelled, rejected or times out after 180 seconds, nothing is stored. If a refresh fails, the stored tokens are cleared and you are asked to sign in again.

docs.title: How sign-in stays secure
docs.text:
• The add-in listens on 127.0.0.1 only, for that one redirect, and checks the state value to reject forged redirects.
  • It uses PKCE and sends no client secret.
  • Tokens are never written to the configuration file or to logs.
Platform Where tokens are stored Windows Encrypted with Windows DPAPI for your user account, in a file under %LOCALAPPDATA%\MfgToFm. macOS Your login Keychain.

docs.title: Permissions in Fusion Manage
docs.text:
Signing in proves who you are. It does not give you access to anything in Fusion Manage. What you can do is decided by the permissions your Fusion Manage user holds in the Items workspace, which are set by your Fusion Manage administrator through your role. The add-in reads them from Fusion Manage each time it needs them, and never changes them.

Ask your Fusion Manage administrator, not the add-in

If something is refused, the add-in cannot grant the permission. Send your administrator the permission names from the message, and ask for them on the Items workspace.

What each task needs

Task Permissions required in the Items workspace Choose the Items workspace in Preferences View Items, Add Items, Edit Items, View BOM, Add To BOM and Edit BOM Publish a design as new and updated items, and their BOMs The same six Open an item in the Item Panel View Items Attach a STEP file or a drawing PDF View Items, Add Attachments and Edit Attachments, in the workspace the file goes to (the Items workspace, or the Components workspace for a component)

The first two rows ask for all six, whether or not a given publish adds or changes anything. This is because the BOM is always published. Within that, creating an item needs Add Items, updating one needs Edit Items, and BOM lines need Add To BOM and Edit BOM. See Publishing.

Tabs in the Item Panel

A tab you lack the permission for is greyed out, rather than hidden. Hover over it to see "Insufficient permissions".

Tab Permission Item View Items Files View Attachments BOM View BOM Where Used View Where Used Workflows View Associated Workflow Changelog View Change Log

If a permission is missing

The message names what is missing, for example:

Insufficient permissions to publish to the Items workspace. Missing: Add Items, Edit BOM.

In Preferences, choosing a workspace you lack permissions on says "You need these permissions on workspace: ...". If Fusion Manage refuses the check outright, the message says "Insufficient permissions" without a list. Either way, ask your administrator to add the permissions to your role, then try again.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Continue to Configuration, where you choose the Items workspace, map fields to it and set where exported files are attached. To see what the add-in reads from your design first, read Manufacturing Data Model.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
In one sentence: the add-in copies a released design from Fusion into Fusion Manage, as a manufacturing item with its parts list (BOM) and files, when you tell it to.

Engineers keep working in Fusion. Manufacturing, purchasing and quality teams work from the item in Fusion Manage. Unfamiliar words are explained in the Glossary.

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text:
• Sign in to Fusion Manage from Fusion with your Autodesk account (Installation).
  • Choose which design properties fill which Fusion Manage fields (Configuration).
  • Create and update items from a design, matched by item number (Publishing).
  • Compare and synchronise the BOM between the design and Fusion Manage (Bill of Materials).
  • Attach a STEP file or drawing PDF to an item, only when you choose to (STEP File, Drawing Representation).
  • Review an item inside Fusion: fields, files, BOM, where-used and workflows (Item Panel).
  • Follow your publishes and retry a failed one (Job Queue).

docs.title: Why it exists
docs.text:
Engineering and the enterprise work to different rhythms. Engineers iterate on designs, while manufacturing, purchasing, quality and supply chain teams need a stable, controlled record of what is to be built. Mixing the two forces one side to inherit the other's pace and permissions.

The add-in keeps them separate by design:

  • Engineering components stay in Fusion, where design work continues and revisions are managed.
  • Manufactured items live in Fusion Manage, each with its own lifecycle, approvals and release status.
  • The add-in is the controlled bridge between them. Fusion and Fusion Manage each keep doing their own job, and information crosses only when you choose to publish.

The result is a single, traceable path from a released design to an item the enterprise can rely on, without re-keying data or maintaining parallel spreadsheets. The End-to-End Workflow shows how this works in practice.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: The add-in reads a design's components, BOM structure, properties, thumbnails and part numbers from the Manufacturing Data Model and compares them with what already exists in Fusion Manage. It shows you the differences before anything changes, then sends only what needs to be created or updated. Nothing is overwritten blindly, and you stay in control of every publish.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
The add-in takes what the design says in the Manufacturing Data Model, compares it with Fusion Manage, and sends only the difference.

Fusion stores its components, BOM and properties in the Manufacturing Data Model. 2 The add-in reads the BOM and each component's properties, thumbnail and part number from the Manufacturing Data Model. 3 Only after the item has been published. When you attach a technical representation, the add-in has Fusion export a STEP file or a drawing PDF and attaches it to the item. 4 The add-in reads the matching items and BOMs in Fusion Manage, shows you the differences, and on your command creates or updates items, BOM lines and attachments.

One sign-in covers both the Data Model and Fusion Manage. It is explained step by step in Installation and Authentication.

Items are matched by item number, which the add-in reads from the component's Item Number in the Manufacturing Data Model. If an item with that number already exists in Fusion Manage it is updated; otherwise it is created.

docs.title: The user interface
docs.text:
The add-in adds an Export panel and an Item Management panel to the Manage tab of the ribbon in the Design and Drawing workspaces. Administration is a submenu of Item Management; its buttons are pinned to the ribbon.

Panel Button Purpose Export Export Open the Export window: export the open design or drawing and attach the file to its item or component Item Management Open Fusion Manage Item Show the item of the selected component, or of the open design or drawing Item Management Publish Fusion Manage Item (Design only) Preview and publish the open design Item Management ▸ Administration Job Queue See publishes that are waiting, running and finished Item Management ▸ Administration Preferences Sign in, set the connection and the workspace mapping

Most buttons stay greyed out until the Items workspace is configured (see Item Workspace). The tooltip of a greyed-out button says why.

docs.title: Using the right-click menu
docs.text:
The same actions are available from the context (right-click) menu of a component, so you can work without leaving the model.

  1. In the Browser (or on the canvas), find the component you want to work with.
  2. Right-click the component to open its context menu.

  3. Choose one of the Fusion Manage entries:

    Menu entry What it does Open Fusion Manage Item Opens the component's linked item in Fusion Manage. Publish Fusion Manage Item Publishes the component and its structure. Available on the top-level component only. Export STEP File Exports the component as a STEP file. Export PDF Exports the drawing as a PDF. Shown only when a drawing is open.

Note

Entries that don't apply to the selected component, or that are unavailable until the Items workspace is configured, are greyed out or hidden.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Autodesk Fusion on Windows or macOS.
  • A Fusion Manage tenant and a user with permission to work in the target workspace.
  • An Autodesk Platform Services (APS) application registered for sign-in (see Installation and Authentication).

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: The add-in works with a single Fusion Manage workspace, Items. See Troubleshooting and Limitations for what is not yet supported. Get the latest version from the Releases page.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Install the add-in and sign in.

docs.title: The problem it solves
docs.text:
Engineering and manufacturing both work on the same product, but they work in different ways.

  • Engineers change designs often. They try ideas, revise parts and release new versions.
  • Manufacturing needs a steady record of what to build. It cannot build from a design that may change tomorrow.

When both teams share one record, each is slowed down by the other. Engineers wait on manufacturing approvals, or manufacturing builds from something that has moved on.

docs.title: The solution: two separate records
docs.text:
The add-in keeps the two apart and joins them only when someone chooses to.

Engineering Manufacturing Lives in Fusion Fusion Manage Record The design: component and drawing The item: a manufacturing record with its own BOM Owned by Engineers Manufacturing Responsible for Design changes and the design's own lifecycle Saying "we are ready to build this now"

Engineering is only responsible for the design and its lifecycle. Engineers design, revise and release in Fusion, and nobody waits on them.

Manufacturing takes a released design and creates an item from it. The item is Manufacturing's signal that we are ready to build this now. Manufacturing can then extend the item's bill of materials (BOM) with what production needs, such as packaging, fasteners and consumables, and release it through its own workflow.

The add-in is the bridge. A component's item number in Fusion is the item number in Fusion Manage. If an item with that number exists it is updated. Otherwise it is created.

docs.title: The benefits
docs.text:
• Engineers are never blocked. They release and revise without waiting for Manufacturing.
  • Manufacturing builds from a stable record. The item changes only when someone publishes, so it does not move under them.
  • Each side keeps its own lifecycle. A design revision does not force an item revision, and the reverse.
  • The BOM can be extended. Manufacturing adds lines the design does not have, and a later publish keeps them.
  • No re-keying. Data moves across, not through spreadsheets or copy and paste.
  • Safe to repeat. Publishing again sends only the differences, so you can bring the item up to date at any time.
  • Ready for the wider business. A released manufacturing item is the right starting point to pass to ERP for work orders, and then to selling. This add-in does not connect to ERP today. It makes the item that a future connection would use.

The add-in does not enforce this process

It will publish any design you open, whatever its state, and it does not release items or start workflows. This is how it is meant to be used. Your organisation's own release rules still apply.
