docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The add-in is installed and you are signed in (Installation and Authentication).
  • The Items workspace is configured (Configuration).
  • Whoever publishes holds the Fusion Manage permissions.

docs.title: 1. Engineering releases the design
docs.text:
Who: Engineering. Where: Fusion.

Engineers model the component, make the drawing and release both as they always do. The add-in is not involved and asks nothing more of them.

Before the next stage, check that:

  • The design and drawing are saved and released.
  • Every component that should become an item has an item number, including the top-level one.

Outcome: a released design that is ready to publish.

docs.title: 2. Publish the item
docs.text:
Who: the Design Engineer or the Manufacturing Engineer. Where: Fusion.

This is the step that crosses from engineering to manufacturing.

  1. Open the released design.
  2. Right-click the top-level component and choose Publish Fusion Manage Item.
  3. Check the BOM. Anything marked New or Update will change in Fusion Manage.
  4. Click Publish, and follow it in the Job Queue.
Sent to the item Not sent The properties you have mapped, and the thumbnail Fields you have not mapped, and the item's lifecycle and workflow, which Fusion Manage owns The design's BOM structure and quantities STEP files and drawing PDFs (you upload these in stage 3)

Keep the two lifecycles apart

You can map Fusion's Revision or Lifecycle state. If you do, map them to informational fields, such as a text field for the engineering revision. Do not map them to the field that drives the item's own lifecycle.

Full steps are in Publishing.

Outcome: each component is an item in Fusion Manage, with its properties, thumbnail and BOM.

docs.title: 3. Extend the manufacturing item
docs.text:
Who: Manufacturing. Where: Fusion and Fusion Manage.

The published item is the starting point. Manufacturing now adds what it needs to build the product.

Task How Extend the BOM with items that are not in the design Use Add Existing Items, then publish again (Bill of Materials). Keep or remove lines that only Fusion Manage has Review the Fusion Manage Only lines. They are kept unless you remove them. Attach a STEP file Select the component and choose Export STEP File (STEP File). Attach a drawing PDF Open the drawing and choose Export PDF (Drawing Representation). Add information that engineering does not supply Edit it in Fusion Manage.

Files are never added automatically

A publish does not attach a STEP file or a PDF. You choose which files go to the supply chain, for which items, and when. Uploading a file that is already attached creates a new version.

Outcome: the item has a complete BOM and the files manufacturing needs.

docs.title: 4. Review
docs.text:
Who: Engineering, Quality and Manufacturing. Where: Fusion or Fusion Manage.

Each group checks the item against the design. In Fusion, select the component and choose Open Fusion Manage Item. Anyone without the add-in can review the same item in Fusion Manage.

Group Check Engineering The Item tab and Bill of Materials tab match the design. Quality The Files tab has the STEP file and drawing PDF. Manufacturing The BOM is complete, and Where Used shows the assemblies that hold the item. Everyone Associated Workflows shows any change orders in progress.

See Item Panel for what each tab shows.

If you find a problem, fix it where it starts. A design problem is fixed in Fusion, released and published again. A manufacturing problem is fixed in Fusion Manage.

Outcome: everyone agrees the item is correct and complete.

docs.title: 5. Manufacturing releases the item
docs.text:
Who: Release approvers. Where: Fusion Manage.

Releasing the item is Manufacturing's statement that we are ready to build this now. It is done through the item's own workflow in Fusion Manage, separate from the engineering release. The add-in does not move an item through its workflow.

  1. In the Item panel, click Open in browser.
  2. In Fusion Manage, run the workflow action your organisation uses to release the item.
  3. Back in Fusion, click Refresh in the Item panel to see the new state.

Outcome: the item is released. A released item is the record that can later pass to ERP for work orders and sales.

docs.title: When the design changes
docs.text: Engineering can keep revising after the item is released, and the item does not change until someone publishes. When Manufacturing needs it brought up to date, publish again. Items that already match are left alone, only the differences are sent, and what Manufacturing added in Fusion Manage is kept.

docs.title: Quick reference
docs.text: I want to… Use Create or update items from a released design Publish Fusion Manage Item See whether a publish worked Job Queue Retry after a failure Retry in the Job Queue Attach a STEP file Export STEP File Attach a drawing PDF Export PDF Review an item Open Fusion Manage Item Release an item Fusion Manage, through Open in browser

docs.title: Item Panel
docs.text:
What you'll do here: check an item's Fusion Manage record without leaving Fusion.

The Item Panel shows an item's Fusion Manage record inside Fusion, next to the design it came from. You can check a publish and see where an item stands in its lifecycle without switching to the browser.

Quick steps: select a component, choose Manage ▸ Item Management ▸ Open Fusion Manage Item, then use the tabs to check fields, files, BOM, where-used and workflows.

It is for reviewing

The panel reads the item. It does not move it through its workflow, and its only change to the item is attaching files you choose to upload. Release happens in Fusion Manage. See Review and Release.

docs.title: Open the Item Panel
docs.text:
• Select a component and choose Manage ▸ Item Management ▸ Open Fusion Manage Item, or right-click the component and choose Open Fusion Manage Item.
  • With nothing selected, the panel shows the item of the open design (or, in a drawing, of the design the drawing shows).

The add-in finds the component you selected by its part number in the open design, reads that component's item number from the Manufacturing Data Model, and looks the item up in the Items workspace by that item number. The panel is drawn by the add-in from the item's own sections and fields, so it needs no separate web sign-in.

The panel follows your selection. While it is open, selecting another component shows that component's item.

If no item has the number, the panel says No Item Exists In Fusion Manage Yet, shows the item number, and lists what publishing will do: open the Publish panel to review what will be sent, create the item in the Items workspace with the design's properties, and add its bill of materials if it is an assembly. Click Publish to Fusion Manage to open the Publish panel. If you may not view the workspace, it tells you so.

docs.title: When several items share the number
docs.text:
If more than one item in the Items workspace has the component's item number, the panel does not guess. In place of the item it lists them, each with its descriptor and Item ID. Click the one you mean.

  • Your choice is remembered for that item number until Fusion closes. It also decides which item a STEP file or drawing is attached to from the panel.
  • A button that appears in the header (two arrows) shows the list again, so you can choose another.
  • If the Fusion Manage search returns look-alike descriptors (PN-1001 - A and PN-10010 - B for PN-1001), the one whose descriptor starts with exactly the item number is used, and you are not asked.
  • Better, give every item its own number. Two items with one number are a data problem in Fusion Manage, and publishing skips such a component until you choose.

docs.title: Header
docs.text: Control What it does Title and status line The item's title, and a line with its version, lifecycle state and Type. Up-to-date check (at the right end of the tabs) A small circle turns while the panel compares the item's mapped fields with the open design, the same comparison the Publish panel makes. When all is well it disappears; when something differs it becomes an amber OUT OF DATE pill, and a red CHECK FAILED pill if the check could not be made. Click the pill to open a dialog that lists what differs (each field with what the open design holds beside what Fusion Manage holds, or each component with its two quantities) and has a Republish button that opens the Publish panel; for a failed check it gives the reason. Hover the pill for a short summary. The mark belongs to the tab shown, and the Item and Bill of Materials tabs have a check so far: the other tabs show no mark. (The Files tab marks out-of-date files on their own rows instead; see Files.) It is checked once each time the item is read in full (opening it, Refresh, an upload), not when you click the Item tab again. It is not shown for a component below the top of the design. Open in browser Opens the item in Fusion Manage in your web browser. Choose another item Shown only when several items share the number. Lists them again so you can pick a different one. Refresh Reads the item again from Fusion Manage. Actions (⋯) Uploads the technical representation: Export STEP File in a design, or the drawing PDF in a drawing. See STEP File and Drawing Representation. In a design the menu also has Republish, which opens the Publish panel.

docs.title: Required permission
docs.text: Reading an item needs View Items in the Items workspace. Without it the panel shows Insufficient permissions to view the Items workspace.

docs.title: Tabs
docs.text:
The tabs are named as Fusion Manage names them and show a count where there is one. A tab your user or workspace does not have is hidden, and one you may not use is disabled. Tabs other than Item are read from Fusion Manage the first time you open them.

Tab Shows Item The item's fields Files Attached files Bill of Materials The item's BOM lines Where Used The assemblies that hold the item Associated Workflows Workflow items that reference the item Change Log What was done to the item, and by whom

docs.title: Item
docs.text: The item's sections and fields as label and value, and matrices as grids. Sections can be collapsed. Images show as thumbnails; click one to enlarge it. Fields the workspace hides are not shown.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
The files attached to the item, with a type icon, sortable by any column. This is where you check that a STEP file or drawing PDF arrived. Empty state: No files attached.

A bar over the table, on the right as in the Bill of Materials, has a button for each file the open document can be exported as and attached to the item: Export STEP File in a design, Export PDF, Export DWG and Export DXF in a drawing, each with its file-type icon. They do the same as the entries of the Actions menu, including the progress dialog, and are greyed while an upload is under way. The bar is hidden when the open document offers nothing.

A file made from the open document is marked Out of Date (an amber label to the left of its icon) when that document was saved after the file was uploaded: the STEP file when a design is open, and the PDF, DWG and DXF when a drawing is open. It is the same check the Export window makes, against the latest saved version of the document. Hover the label for the dates. A document with unsaved changes marks them too, as the file cannot show changes that were never saved.

docs.title: Bill of Materials
docs.text:
The item's lines as a tree, with the same columns as Fusion Manage's own BOM view, a Views selector and a column chooser. Use it to check the BOM you published. See Bill of Materials. Empty state: No Bill of Materials.

Each time the tab is opened, the mark at the right of the tab bar compares the open design's components with this Bill of Materials, as the Publish panel does: OUT OF DATE when a component of the design is not under the same parent here, or is there in another quantity (click the pill for the components and their quantities). Nothing shows when it is up to date. Lines only Fusion Manage has, such as manufacturing lines added there, are not a difference. It is shown only for the top of the design.

docs.title: Where Used
docs.text: The assemblies that hold the item, as a tree. Expand a parent to read the next level up. Empty state: Not used in any assembly.

docs.title: Associated Workflows
docs.text:
The tab takes its name from your Fusion Manage workspace. In the example above it reads Change Processes, with the number of workflow items beside it.

The workflow items, such as change orders, that reference the item. Each row shows the workflow item's current state and its last workflow step: when, by whom, the action taken and any comments. Empty state: No associated workflows.

docs.title: Change Log
docs.text: What was done to the item, newest first: when, by whom, the action, and a description. Fields a change edited are listed under the description with the old value struck through and the new value beside it. The first 100 entries are read, and more are read as you scroll towards the end (a progress bar shows while they load). Only the rows in view are drawn, so a long log stays smooth. Needs the View Change Log permission. Empty state: No changes logged.

docs.title: Review after a publish
docs.text:
Open the item in the Item Panel and work through the tabs:

  1. Check the Item tab fields against the design.
  2. Check Files for the STEP file or drawing PDF you attached.
  3. Check Bill of Materials against the design BOM you published.
  4. Check Where Used to confirm the item sits in the right assembly.
  5. Check Associated Workflows to see whether a change order already covers the item and where it is.

Each tab is described in Tabs. Anyone without the add-in can review the same item in Fusion Manage directly.

If the review finds a problem, correct it at its source. A design problem is fixed in Fusion, released, and published again. A manufacturing problem is fixed in Fusion Manage. Then review again.

docs.title: Release happens in Fusion Manage
docs.text:
The manufactured item is released through a change order in Fusion Manage, independent of the engineering release in Fusion. The add-in does not move an item through its workflow, and it does not create the change order.

  1. In the Item Panel, click Open in browser to go straight to the item, or open Fusion Manage yourself.
  2. In Fusion Manage, create a Change Order.
  3. In the change order, Add Affected Manufacturing Items and choose the item you published.
  4. Run the change order through its workflow. When the change order is released, the item it covers is released with it.
  5. Back in Fusion, click Refresh to see the item's new state, or check the Associated Workflows tab: the change order is listed there with its current state and last step.

For how this fits into the wider process, see the End-to-End Workflow.

docs.title: Job Queue
docs.text:
What you'll do here: see whether a publish worked, and retry it if it did not.

Every publish is a job. The Job Queue shows the jobs that are waiting, running and finished, so you can see what the add-in is doing without keeping the Publish panel open.

Quick steps: open it with Manage ▸ Item Management ▸ Administration ▸ Job Queue. Click a job to see the reason for a failure. To send a failed job again, see Retry a failed run.

docs.title: How jobs run
docs.text: Jobs go through a single queue, one after another. A publish returns at once, and the work happens in the background, so Fusion stays responsive and you can keep working, even in another design. A job that is waiting shows its place, for example Waiting, number 2 in the queue.

docs.title: Reading the queue
docs.text:
The panel is a table of every job that is waiting, running, failed or cancelled, newest first, one row per job. A job that went through leaves the list.

Column What it shows Status A pill with an icon and the status in words, the same width for every job Job The name of the job, the design it publishes Progress A sentence on where it stands, for example Checking item numbers., Publishing 4 of 5 items., Updating the Bill of Materials, 12 of 40 requests., Cancelled. Nothing was published. or Failed. 2 of 12 items failed. Time How long the job has taken, counting up while it runs. A dash while it waits Cancel while it is waiting or running, Retry once it has failed

Click a row for its details. A window opens over the Job Queue with the result in words, the time it took, and a table of the job's items:

  • Filters above the table show all items, or only the failed, skipped, cancelled, running, waiting or done ones, with how many there are of each. A job with failures opens on the failed items. Find an item narrows the table by item number or description.
  • Click an item to see its details beside the table: its number, description, status and publish, and under them the reason in full when it failed, was skipped or was cancelled.
  • Retry and Cancel publish are in the window too. Close it with Close, Esc, or by clicking outside it.
Status Meaning Queued Waiting for earlier jobs to finish Running Being prepared or sent Failed Failed, or finished with failed rows. The full reason is in the job's details Cancelled Stopped before it finished

In a job's details, each BOM sent for a parent assembly also has its own line, after the items.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
• Cancel stops a job that is waiting or running. Items already processed are kept in the run's folder, and the rest are not published. The job stays listed as Cancelled, and the message at the top of the Job Queue says how many cancelled publishes are waiting to be cleared.
  • Clear finished removes finished jobs from the list, and their files with them: a cleared job can no longer be retried. A job that finished with every row done removes itself.
  • Retry appears on a job that failed or has failed rows. It sends the failed requests again. See Request Files and Retry.

docs.title: Knowing when something ends
docs.text:
You do not have to watch the panel.

  • The Job Queue button on the ribbon changes its icon. A green dot means a publish is waiting or running, a red dot means a listed job has failed, and the plain clock means nothing is running. The tooltip says which.
  • When a job ends, a message box reports the result. A publish that completed shows Total Items Processed, Total Items Created and Total Items Updated. A failure lists the items that failed and why. This appears even if the Publish and Job Queue panels are closed.

docs.title: A failed job
docs.text:
A failed job stays in the Job Queue, marked Failed, until you clear it. Click it to open its details, which show what happened to every item in the job.

  1. Open the Job Queue and click the failed job. The details open on the Failed items.
  2. Click an item in the table. Its Reason shows beside the table, in full.
  3. Fix the cause in Fusion or Fusion Manage.
  4. Click Retry, on the job's row or in its details. What Fusion Manage already accepted is skipped.

Choose All above the table to see the items that went through too. For common causes, see Troubleshooting and Limitations.

docs.title: What a run keeps
docs.text:
Every publish writes its files to a temporary folder (MfgToFm under the system temp folder) while it runs. The add-in removes only folders inside it, and nothing else.

  • A run that goes through is removed when it ends, because everything was sent and there is nothing left to retry.
  • A run that fails, has failed rows or is cancelled keeps its folder, so you can read it and use Retry.
  • Clear finished removes those folders along with the jobs.

The path is listed in Troubleshooting and Limitations. Each run has its own folder, containing:

File What it holds Per-item request JSON The exact request written for each item, a create or an update Thumbnails The images downloaded for the items bom/ The BOM requests for each parent assembly manifest.json A summary of the run send-log.json A record of every request Fusion Manage accepted

The files are what the retry below works from, and a record of what was sent for a run that did not go through.

docs.title: Retry a failed run
docs.text:
1. Open the Job Queue.
  2. Click Retry on the failed job.

The retry replaces the failed job in the list and sends the run's folder again, as a new job. It does not ask for confirmation, because it sends the same requests the run already wrote.

docs.title: Nothing is sent twice
docs.text:
What Fusion Manage already accepted is skipped. The send-log.json in the folder records each accepted request, so sending a folder again carries on from where it stopped instead of creating items twice.

An item whose creation failed is not there for its BOM, so that BOM fails too. The other items carry on. After you fix the cause and click Retry, the item and then its BOM go through.

docs.title: Folders it will not send
docs.text: If the run's folder is missing or cannot be read (for example the run failed before it wrote its files), Retry says why in a message box. In that case, publish again.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text:
What you'll do here: turn a released design into manufacturing items in Fusion Manage, then attach STEP files and drawings.

Items and BOMs are sent by Publish. STEP files and drawing PDFs are different: they are never sent by a publish and are uploaded one at a time by you. See Technical representations are manual.

docs.title: Quick steps
docs.text:
1. Open the saved design.
  2. Right-click the top-level component and choose Publish Fusion Manage Item.
  3. Check the BOM and the New or Update marks in the Details Panel.
  4. Click Publish, and follow it in the Job Queue.
  5. Optional: attach a STEP file or drawing PDF.

Review the result in the Item Panel.

docs.title: In this page
docs.text: Section Read it when Open the Publish panel and Publish You are publishing for the first time. Item Creation and Item Update You want to know what is created, changed or never overwritten. Bill of Materials You are comparing or editing the BOM. STEP File and Drawing Representation You are attaching files.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You are signed in and the Items workspace is configured (Installation and Authentication, Item Workspace).
  • The design is saved and its components have item numbers. Items in Fusion Manage are matched by item number.
  • Your Fusion Manage user holds the permissions listed in the Items workspace: View Items, Add Items, Edit Items, View BOM, Add To BOM and Edit BOM. Otherwise the panel shows a "no access" message naming what is missing.

docs.title: Open the Publish panel
docs.text:
Publishing always starts from the top of the design, so open the design first (a drawing cannot be published). There is no Publish button on the ribbon. Use either of these:

  1. From the design. Right-click the top-level component in the browser and choose Publish Fusion Manage Item. The entry is offered on the top-level component only.

  2. From the Item panel. Select the component and choose Open Fusion Manage Item, then do one of the following:

    • If the item is not in Fusion Manage yet, click Publish to Fusion Manage.
    • Open the Actions (...) menu and choose Republish. It is offered whenever a design is open.
    • If the tab's pill shows Out of date, click it to open the report, then click Republish.

    The Item panel closes as the Publish panel opens.

The panel shows the design's thumbnail and summary, and below it the Bill of Materials of the design compared with Fusion Manage. The thumbnail arrives a moment after the rest, so you can start on the BOM while it loads. Click a row to open the Details Panel beside it, which shows the item, a status pill at its top right, and a table of its properties with the value in Fusion, the value in Fusion Manage and a status dot for each. Hover a dot to see what publishing will do for that property. A row's details are read when you open it, and the design's own row reads its properties the first time you open it.

docs.title: Status in the Details Panel
docs.text:
The pill at the top right of the Details Panel shows what publishing will do for the component:

Status Meaning New No item exists in Fusion Manage yet; publishing creates it. See Item Creation. Update The Fusion Manage value differs; publishing changes it. See Item Update. Up to date The mapped property values already match. A default value to send again, or a missing component link, is not shown here but is still sent with a publish. Shared number Several Fusion Manage items have this number. Fix it in Fusion Manage: publishing fails until then. Error Fusion Manage could not be read for this item.

Properties with no mapping are listed as not published. Mapped properties are listed first so you see what will change.

docs.title: Publish
docs.text:
1. Review the BOM and details. Refresh reads the design and Fusion Manage again.
  2. Optionally use Add Existing Items to include existing Fusion Manage items in the BOM (see Bill of Materials).
  3. Click Publish. The button is enabled once the BOM has loaded. It stays disabled while a line still needs a choice (Review), while Expand all is reading the tree, and when the design's own item number is shared.

A progress dialog appears with up to three bars, one after the other, each with a percentage. Reading shows only when the Bill of Materials has levels that are not read yet: Publish reads and compares them first, counting the lines so far, and the bar turns green with the number of items found when it is done. Validating looks up every item number in Fusion Manage. If a number belongs to several items, or Fusion Manage cannot be searched, the run stops there and nothing is written (see Item numbers that several items carry). Once validation is complete and green, Publishing fills as the items are created or updated and then as the requests of the Bill of Materials are sent (each add, update, removal or renumber counts as one). You can close it; the run continues in the background and you can keep working in Fusion, even in another design. Closing it while Reading is still going drops the publish. Use Cancel publish to stop: items already processed are kept in the run's folder, the rest are not published.

Under the bars the dialog shows the time elapsed and a tally of Successful, Failed and Pending items. A Skipped box is added when items were left out on purpose.

docs.title: What a run does
docs.text:
1. Reads each item's properties from the Data Model and compares them with Fusion Manage (up to five items at once).
  2. Downloads the thumbnail, for each item that is created or updated. It is attached only when a thumbnail is mapped to an image field; otherwise nothing is downloaded.
  3. Writes a request file for each item, then sends it: a POST creates an item, a PATCH updates one.
  4. Once every item exists, sends the BOM changes of each parent assembly. BOMs go last so that new parents and children already have IDs. Removals, updates and renumbers go first, up to five requests at a time; once they are all done, the adds follow, also up to five at a time. A line is therefore freed before another takes its position.

When the run ends, the progress dialog turns into the result. It reads Publish complete when every item went through, Completed with errors when some failed (see the Job Queue for the reasons), Publish cancelled after Cancel publish, Validation failed when the item numbers could not be checked or several items carry one (Publishing shows Not started), or Publish failed when the run could not finish after validation.

If you closed the dialog, Fusion shows a message box instead when the run completes or completes with errors (titled Publish completed with errors; nothing is shown for a cancelled run), with Total Items Processed, Total Items Created and Total Items Updated, and, for any failure, the item and the reason.

The run itself is shown in the Job Queue, and if something fails you can send it again with Request Files and Retry.

docs.title: Technical representations are manual
docs.text: A publish sends item data, the BOM and the thumbnail. It does not attach a STEP file or a drawing PDF. Those are uploaded manually, so you decide what goes to the supply chain, for which items, and when. See STEP File and Drawing Representation.

docs.title: What is and is not sent
docs.text:
• Mapped properties with no value in the Data Model are never sent. On a create the run records "No value in the Data Model, not sent" with the field names. On an update, a value Fusion Manage already holds is kept: Fusion having none never clears it. Only a real difference, such as Steel in Fusion and Plastic in Fusion Manage, is pushed.
  • Properties are only ever added or changed. The add-in does not delete items, and removes a BOM line only when you choose Remove on it.
  • A component whose item number is shared with another component is not published. See Shared item numbers.

docs.title: Item Creation
docs.text: When a component has no item in Fusion Manage yet, publishing creates one.

docs.title: When an item is created
docs.text:
For each component in the Publish panel, the add-in searches the Items workspace for an item with the component's item number. If nothing is found, the Details Panel shows New for it and a publish creates it. A design that is not in Fusion Manage at all has no status on its BOM lines, because there is nothing to compare them with. If an item is found, see Item Update.

The search is by item number only. Make sure your workspace maps Item Number to the Fusion Manage field that holds it (NUMBER in the default mapping). In Fusion Manage, that field must also be part of the Items workspace's item descriptor, or existing items are not found. See The item number.

docs.title: What a new item receives
docs.text:
A new item is created with:

Content Where it comes from Every mapped property that has a value The Manufacturing Data Model, through your field mapping Every default value Your workspace settings. Default values are set on every new item The thumbnail The Data Model, when the thumbnail is mapped to an image field The component link The Fusion Manage component for the part, when a linking field is chosen

How values are prepared:

  • Picklist fields receive the matching option. A value that matches no option is left out and recorded, and the rest of the item is still created. See Picklists.
  • Number fields are rounded to the precision the Fusion Manage field takes.
  • Empty values are not sent. The run records No value in the Data Model, not sent, with the field names.

docs.title: Order of creation
docs.text:
Every component is created or updated first, then the BOM lines are sent. A BOM line needs both the parent and the child to exist, so BOMs always go last. See Bill of Materials.

If an item fails to be created, the other items carry on. The failed item's BOM is skipped, because the item is not there for it. You can retry from the Job Queue: what Fusion Manage already accepted is skipped, so nothing is created twice.

docs.title: Permission needed
docs.text: Creating an item needs Add Items in the Items workspace.

docs.title: What does not happen
docs.text: Creating an item does not attach a STEP file or a drawing PDF. Those are uploaded by you afterwards, only for the items you choose. See STEP File and Drawing Representation.

docs.title: After creation
docs.text: The run reports Total Items Created. Open the new item in the Item Panel to check it.

docs.title: Item Update
docs.text: When a component already has an item in Fusion Manage, publishing updates it, and only where something differs. Publishing the same design twice is safe.

docs.title: When an item is updated
docs.text:
The add-in searches the Items workspace for the component's item number.

Result of the search What happens One item found The item is compared with the design and updated where needed No item found The item is created. See Item Creation Several items found The status is Shared number. The run fails before it writes anything: fix the number in Fusion Manage (see Item numbers that several items carry)

docs.title: What an update sends
docs.text:
An update sends only what has changed:

  • Mapped properties whose values differ. These are the ones marked Update in the Details Panel.
  • Default values the item does not hold. A default value is sent again when the item's field does not hold it, so a value someone changed in Fusion Manage is set back to the default. A field already holding the default is left alone.
  • The component link, if the item lacks it.
  • The thumbnail. Images cannot be compared, so the thumbnail is sent with every update, even when nothing else differs. An item with a mapped thumbnail is therefore updated by every publish.

If nothing differs and no thumbnail is mapped (or the component has none yet), no request is sent and the run records Fusion Manage already has the same values. Such an item is not counted as updated.

Numbers are compared at the precision of the Fusion Manage field. If the field already holds the number at its precision, it is not sent again.

docs.title: What is never overwritten
docs.text:
An update never changes:

  • A value Fusion Manage holds where Fusion has none. Publishing never blanks a field.
  • Fields you have not mapped. Anything entered in Fusion Manage that is not part of the mapping is untouched. This is how the manufacturing information added after publishing survives a later publish.
  • The item's lifecycle state and workflow. Fusion Manage owns them.
  • BOM lines that only Fusion Manage has. They are kept unless you choose to remove them. See Bill of Materials.

Engineering changes

When a design changes after it was published, publish again. Items that still match are skipped, items that differ are updated, and what Manufacturing added in Fusion Manage is preserved.

docs.title: Item numbers that several items carry
docs.text:
The add-in asks Fusion Manage for items whose descriptor matches the component's item number, and uses the item when exactly one comes back. When more than one comes back it does not guess, and nothing can be published until the number belongs to one item. This happens when two items in the workspace carry the same item number. Fusion Manage does not stop that, for example when items were created by hand or imported. The fix is in Fusion Manage: renumber or remove the extra items, then refresh the panel.

  • In the panel. Open the component's details. The status is Shared number, and the Details Panel lists the Fusion Manage items that carry the number. A design whose own number is shared is not compared: the Bill of Materials says so, and Publish and Add Existing Items stay disabled.
  • When you publish. Before anything is written, the run looks up every item number in Fusion Manage. If any number is carried by several items, the whole run fails and nothing is published. The progress dialog shows the Validating bar failed and Publishing not started. While the numbers are looked up, each row of the Bill of Materials shows a spinner, then a green tick, or a red cross when several items carry its number. The crosses stay after the failure, and the panel does not refresh, so you can find the items to fix. The run does not appear in the Job Queue. Nothing is partly published, so after you have fixed Fusion Manage you publish again.
  • If the look-up fails. If Fusion Manage cannot be searched, the run fails the same way, because the numbers cannot be known to be unique.

The Item Panel asks which item you mean, and remembers the item you pick. The right-click STEP upload, the drawing upload and the Export window use the Item panel's choice; when several items match and none was chosen they stop with a message and attach nothing.

A BOM line of an assembly that matches several items is left without a status for the same reason. Fix it by removing the duplicate in Fusion Manage.

docs.title: Permission needed
docs.text: Updating an item needs Edit Items in the Items workspace.

docs.title: After the update
docs.text: The run reports Total Items Updated. Open the item in the Item Panel to check the result.

docs.title: Bill of Materials
docs.text: The Publish panel compares the design's BOM with the BOM already in Fusion Manage, line by line, and sends only the differences. You decide how to handle anything that is in Fusion Manage but not in the design.

docs.title: Large designs
docs.text:
The panel reads the BOM one level at a time, so a large assembly opens quickly. At first it shows the design and the lines directly under it. Click an assembly's chevron to read the lines under it: a spinner replaces the chevron and grey rows hold the place until they arrive. If one assembly cannot be read, its rows show Could not read this level with a Retry button, and the rest of the table stays.

Expand all reads every level that is not read yet and opens everything; Collapse all closes every assembly except the design itself.

Publish covers the whole design. If some levels are not read yet, Publish first reads and compares every one of them (as Expand all does), then goes on to validate the item numbers and publish. If that read shows lines that need a choice (Review), they are opened for you and the publish waits; choose, then click Publish again. If the read fails, nothing is published. The pills at the bottom left count what is covered:

Pill Counts Items The design and every component of it: each is checked against Fusion Manage when you publish, and created or updated where it differs. Lines Skipped Lines with no item number (and what is below them): nothing is published for them. Shared Item Numbers Lines whose item number another component also carries (and what is below them): see Shared item numbers.

A line that needs a choice (Review) holds Publish back, whether its assembly is open or closed.

Each read is made a page of 250 lines at a time, and the panel shows how many lines it has read so far. The add-in never shows part of a BOM as if it were all of it. The filter counts and the check button cover only the levels read so far, and say so. If a read is bigger than the add-in can handle, the panel says so instead of showing a table when the first level fails, and shows a message and keeps the table when Expand all fails:

  • More than 25,000 lines in one read (a level, or the whole tree for Expand all).
  • Nested 50 levels deep or more (checked on the whole-tree read).
  • A component that contains itself.

docs.title: How lines are compared
docs.text:
For each parent assembly, the lines of the design are matched to the Fusion Manage lines under that same parent by item number. Repeated item numbers pair one to one in order. Each line gets a status:

Status Meaning Publishing does New The design has the line; Fusion Manage does not. Adds the line. Update Same item, different quantity. Updates the quantity in Fusion Manage. (no chip) Same item and quantity. Nothing. Fusion Manage Only Fusion Manage has a line the design does not. It has no chip of its own; use the Fusion Manage Only filter to find it. Keeps it unless you choose Remove. Review A New line and a Fusion Manage Only line sit under the same parent and need your choice (see Paired rows). Holds Publish back. Keep / Remove Your choice on a Fusion Manage Only line or a pair. Keeps the line, or deletes it. Added You picked the item with Add Existing Items. Adds the line to the end of the Fusion Manage BOM. Skipped The component has no item number, shares one with another component, or sits below such a line. Nothing: no item is created and no BOM line is added.

If an assembly inside the design does not exist in Fusion Manage yet, every child of it is New. If the design itself is not in Fusion Manage, its lines show no status: the panel says publishing creates the design, and does not look up every component. When you publish, each component is searched for by item number, an item that exists is used, and one that does not is created.

Fusion Manage often extends the design BOM with manufacturing lines such as oil or panels. For that reason lines found only in Fusion Manage are never deleted automatically.

Each line reads Item Number - Part Name. A component with no item number is Skipped: no item can be created for it. Its quantity box is greyed out and cannot be edited, and the i on its chip explains why when you hover it. Everything below a skipped assembly is skipped too, because it has no item to join in the Fusion Manage BOM.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
The Filters drop-down above the table (top left) narrows it to rows of one status. Tick any number at once.

  • Statuses you can filter by: Review, New, Added, Update, Fusion Manage Only, Skipped and Duplicates.
  • Counts and tooltips. Each filter shows how many lines it holds, and its tooltip explains what it shows.
  • Show Hidden Components is separate. It adds the components that are hidden in the Fusion component tree, marked with a crossed eye.
  • Clear filters unticks them all.
  • Collapse all and Expand all, next to it at the right, fold the whole tree.

docs.title: Duplicates
docs.text:
Duplicates holds the lines whose item number several Fusion Manage items carry, so you can go straight to the items to fix.

  • When it fills. Only when you click Publish. The Validating step looks up every item number in Fusion Manage, and any number that comes back with several items is added to the filter. Opening the panel or a component's details does not fill it.
  • What you see. The lines appear under the filter, and the same red crosses show on their rows.
  • How long it lasts. Until you refresh the panel, or the next publish checks the numbers again.
  • What to do. Renumber or remove the extra items in Fusion Manage, then publish again.

docs.title: Paired rows: a replaced item
docs.text:
When a New design line and a Fusion Manage Only line sit under the same parent at the same position in the BOM, they are shown paired, one above the other, each carrying the other's item number. The item number differs at that position, which may mean an item was replaced, so the add-in asks you to decide rather than guessing.

Lines at different positions are not paired. For example, if line 11 was removed in Fusion Manage and a line 12 (oil) was added there, the design's line 11 is simply New and the oil line is Fusion Manage Only, kept unless you choose Remove. Nothing needs a choice.

For a pair you can choose:

  • Keep the Fusion Manage line, which is renumbered to the end of the BOM, and add the new design line.
  • Remove the Fusion Manage line from Fusion Manage and add the design's line.

A Fusion Manage Only line with no partner shows a single Remove button; click it again to go back to keeping the line. A line marked for removal is highlighted so you cannot miss it.

docs.title: Editing quantities
docs.text: A quantity can be edited in the table. An edited cell shows a revert button that restores the original value.

docs.title: Add Existing Items
docs.text:
Add Existing Items (top right of the BOM) opens a picker that searches the Items workspace so you can add items that are not in the design.

  • With nothing typed the picker lists every item of the workspace; Search applies the search box and the filters.
  • The search box matches the item descriptor. The Filter pane on the left narrows the results by property: choose a property and a value (a drop-down for properties with a fixed list). Add Row adds another property to the group and Add Group starts a new group. Rows of a group, and groups, are joined by AND or OR; the Items workspace is always applied on top.
  • Results load 25 at a time as you scroll. When some of them are hidden (see below), the picker reads on until it has 25 to show, or the matches run out. The count above the list is of the items it shows, so it ends as, for example, "61 of 61". Tick the items to add; selections survive searching and paging, and Clear unticks them all.
  • The bar under the list shows how many items are selected. Show only selected narrows the list to the ticked items, so you can review them before adding. Cancel closes the picker without adding anything.
  • Items the Bill of Materials already holds, or that you have already added in the panel, are hidden. Turn on Show hidden items to see them ticked, greyed out and locked.
  • Next to Search a version picker chooses the latest or the working version of the items. Add to BOM in the footer adds the ticked items; Show only selected is disabled until something is ticked.
  • Added lines appear in the BOM as Added and can be taken out again with their own Remove button before publishing.

docs.title: What gets sent
docs.text:
Each change becomes one request against the parent item's BOM:

Operation Request Add a line POST to the parent's bom-items Change a quantity PATCH with the new quantity Renumber a kept line PATCH with the new BOM item number Remove a line DELETE

They are ordered so a line is freed before another takes its number: remove, renumber, update, add.

All BOM requests are sent after every item exists, one parent at a time. A failure stops only that parent; the others carry on. Adding a line the BOM already has is reported by Fusion Manage as a duplicate; the add-in logs it and treats it as done, so no failure is recorded. See Request Files and Retry for sending it again.

docs.title: The Export Window
docs.text:
Export (in the Export panel of the Manage tab) opens one small window for every file the add-in can attach. You choose two things:

  1. Attach to. Two cards, at the top. Item attaches the file to the item of the part in the Items workspace. Component attaches it to the part's record in the Components workspace: its working version, when the part has several revisions. When the window opens it checks, in Fusion Manage, that you may attach files to each workspace (View Items, Add Attachments and Edit Attachments; the last is for a new version of a file already there). A card you may not use is greyed out and says why. If the Items workspace is not set up in Preferences, Item says Item is not configured. Complete it in Preferences. and a usable card is chosen for you: the default for that format in Preferences ▸ Export if it can be used, otherwise the first usable one. Component is also greyed out when the connection is invalid or there is no Components workspace.
  2. File format. What the open document can be exported as: a design makes a STEP file; a drawing makes a PDF, DWG or DXF. The window names what is being exported: the selected component of a design (else the whole design), or the top of a drawing.

The window starts with what is being exported: its item number (a grey bar stands there while it is read from Fusion Manage), and under it the description of the design. The attachment card shows whether the file already in Fusion Manage is Up to date, with the date the component was last modified, the file's version, size and who changed it.

Choose Export and the window stays open and shows the progress: Find item, the file being made, and Upload, with a percentage where one can be measured. It then says how it went. On success it reads Export complete with where the file went, and Done closes it. On a failure it reads Export failed with the reason; Try again takes you back to the choices, and Close closes the window. Cancel closes the window before an export starts. The file is named after the item number and a file of the same name is replaced by a new version. See STEP File and Drawing Representation.

The Actions menu of the Item Panel and the right-click entries do not open this window: they export in one step and always attach to the item.

docs.title: STEP File
docs.text:
The add-in can attach a STEP file of a component to its Fusion Manage item, so the wider supply chain has a neutral 3D representation to work from.

Uploaded by you, never automatic

Publishing an item does not attach a STEP file. STEP files are uploaded manually, one component at a time, so you stay in control of what is released, for which items, and when. If you never upload one, none is sent.

The item must already exist. Publish it first (Item Creation).

docs.title: Find the right-click entry
docs.text:
Export STEP File is in the right-click menu of a component. It is the quickest way to upload, with no window to fill in.

  1. Open the saved design in the Design workspace. The entry is not offered in a drawing.
  2. Right-click the component you want, in the browser or on the canvas. Any component works, not only the top one. With nothing selected, the design's top-level component is used.
  3. Choose Export STEP File.

The entry appears only once the add-in is set up. The upload then runs as described below: the item is found by its item number, a STEP file of the selected component is made and attached to that item, and a file already attached with the same name becomes a new version. See New versions, not duplicates.

You can also click Export in the Export panel of the Manage tab on the ribbon. This opens the Export window, where you choose whether to attach to the item or the component, and the file format (STEP for a design). The upload is also in the Actions menu of the Item Panel. The right-click entry and the Actions menu always attach to the item. Only the Export window lets you attach to the component record instead.

docs.title: Upload a STEP file
docs.text:
The file is named after the item number, for example PN-1001.step.

  1. In the Design workspace, select a component in the browser or canvas. With nothing selected, the open design's top-level component is used.
  2. Do one of the following:
    • Right-click and choose Export STEP File (offered on any component, not only the top).
    • Open the item in the Item Panel and choose Actions ▸ Export STEP File.
  3. A small Uploading STEP File window shows three stages: Find item, Create STEP and Upload, with a percentage where one can be measured.
  4. When it finishes you see a confirmation: <name> was attached to the item in Fusion Manage. or A new version of <name> was uploaded to the item in Fusion Manage. It appears as a message box, or as a toast when the Item panel is open.

docs.title: New versions, not duplicates
docs.text: If a file of the same name is already attached, the upload creates a new version of it instead of a duplicate, and the confirmation says so. You can refresh a STEP file as the design changes without cluttering the item.

docs.title: Which geometry is exported
docs.text:
The STEP file contains the selected component, not the whole design.

  • If the selected component is the design's top-level component, the whole design is exported.
  • Otherwise the add-in finds the component in the open design by its part number (the one you selected is tried first) and exports just that.
  • If Fusion cannot export it directly from the open design, the add-in falls back to the component's own document.

The part number only locates the component in Fusion. The item it is attached to is found by the component's item number, read from the Data Model. Finding a component by part number can take a while in large designs. The progress window stays responsive and you will see the percentage move.

docs.title: Messages you may see
docs.text:
• Open the design to publish as a STEP file first. No design is open.
  • Select a component that has a part number, or open a design that has one. The selected component has no part number.
  • No component with part number … in the open design. The selected component's part number is not found in the open design.
  • … has no item number, so it has not been published to Fusion Manage. and The design has not been saved, so it has no item number. The item number cannot be read.
  • No item exists for … No item in Fusion Manage has that item number. Publish the item first.
  • … Fusion Manage items match … Open the item in the Item panel and choose one first. Several items share the item number. Open the item from the Item panel, pick one from the list, and try again.
  • Fusion could not export the STEP file. Fusion refused the export; the message lists each method that was tried (open design, component, own document).

Messages after the item search start with Could not attach a STEP file: or Could not create PN.step:.

Only one upload runs at a time. Starting another reports that a file is already being uploaded.

docs.title: Seeing the result
docs.text: The file appears on the Files tab of the item in the Item Panel. If the panel is open it shows a success toast and re-reads the item, so the file count updates.

docs.title: Drawing Representation
docs.text:
The add-in can attach a PDF of a drawing to the Fusion Manage item of the design the drawing shows, so the supply chain has the released drawing alongside the item.

Uploaded by you, never automatic

Publishing an item does not attach a drawing PDF. Drawing PDFs are uploaded manually, so you decide which drawings go to the supply chain, and when.

A drawing is not an item of its own. Its PDF is attached to the item of the design's top-level component. That item must already exist; publish it first (Item Creation).

docs.title: Upload a drawing PDF
docs.text:
1. Open the drawing. The add-in works out which item it belongs to from the design the drawing references: the part number of that design's top-level component is read, then its item number from the Data Model, and the item with that number is the one used.
  2. Choose Manage ▸ Export ▸ Export and pick PDF, or right-click the top of the drawing's component tree and choose Export PDF. In a drawing, the Item Panel Actions menu offers the same upload.
  3. A PDF of every sheet of the drawing is created, named after the item number (for example PN-1001.pdf), and uploaded in a window with the stages Find item, Create PDF and Upload.

The Export window and the Item Panel's Actions menu can also make a DWG or a DXF of the drawing, attached the same way, as PN-1001.dwg or PN-1001.dxf. The right-click entry makes the PDF only. A Fusion that cannot export those formats says so.

The right-click entry is meant for the top of the tree. It is not offered on an occurrence or on a component other than the design's top-level one, but it can appear for other kinds of selection.

docs.title: New versions, not duplicates
docs.text: If a file of the same name is already attached, the upload creates a new version of it instead of a duplicate.

docs.title: The drawing must be loaded
docs.text: A drawing takes a moment to load. Until its design reference has loaded and the top-level component's part number can be read, the right-click entry is greyed out and its tooltip says what it is waiting for (Not available: followed by a reason such as The drawing has no references yet. or The top-level component of … has no part number.). The add-in checks again when Fusion reports a document or workspace change, or after 15 seconds without one, and gives up after 60 seconds. In the Item panel's Actions menu the entry is disabled with The drawing is still loading and updates when you open the menu or return to the window. The Export window shows The drawing is not ready yet and asks again every 2 seconds.

docs.title: If the PDF is empty
docs.text: Fusion can report an export as successful straight after a drawing opens while writing nothing. The add-in detects this and asks you to wait for the drawing to finish loading and try again.

docs.title: Seeing the result
docs.text: The PDF appears on the Files tab of the item in the Item Panel. If the panel is open it shows a success toast and re-reads the item, so the file count updates.

docs.title: Manufacturing Data Model
docs.text:
What you'll do here: nothing to set. This page explains where the add-in gets its data, and what has to be true of your design before you publish.

The Manufacturing Data Model is the source of everything the add-in publishes. This page explains what it is, what the add-in reads from it, and what has to be true of your design for the data to be there. How that data is matched to Fusion Manage fields is set in Configuration.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
When you save a design in Fusion, Autodesk stores a structured description of it in the cloud: its components, their properties, the BOM structure that relates them, and their thumbnails. That cloud description is the Manufacturing Data Model. It is exposed through an Autodesk Platform Services (APS) API.

The add-in uses it as a read-only source. It never writes to it.

docs.title: Why the add-in reads from the cloud
docs.text:
Reading the cloud description, rather than asking the open Fusion document, has practical benefits:

  • A publish runs in the background. It does not freeze Fusion, and the design does not need to stay open while it runs.
  • Properties of every component, at every level of the assembly, are available without opening each one.
  • The Data Model is read through Fusion itself, as the user Fusion is signed in as, so it needs no Client ID or second login. Writing to Fusion Manage still uses the sign-in set up in Settings.

The add-in reads what has been saved

Because the source is the saved cloud version of the design, changes you have not saved are not seen. A design that Fusion has not finished processing may also be incomplete. Save, and let the design finish processing, before you publish or compare.

docs.title: What the add-in reads
docs.text: Data What it is Used for Component summary The top-level component's item number, part number, description and name Identifying the item, and the title of the Publish panel Properties Every property of a component: base properties that ship with the Data Model and custom properties your organisation has defined The values you map to Fusion Manage fields Physical properties Mass, volume, area, density and the bounding box (length, width, height), worked out from the geometry Mapped fields, when you choose to map them BOM structure Every component below the top level, with quantities and sequence numbers, at any depth up to 50 levels The Bill of Materials comparison and publish Thumbnail An image of each component The item's image field, when mapped Fusion Manage link The Fusion Manage item a component is already linked to, if its Item Number carries that hyperlink in Fusion Component linking when publishing

docs.title: Item number and part number
docs.text:
The Data Model holds two numbers for a component, and the add-in uses them for different things.

Used for Item number Matching. It is the key to everything: it is how the add-in decides whether an item already exists in Fusion Manage, and it is the number the item is created with. A component with no item number cannot be published. Part number Finding the component in Fusion. When you select a component, Fusion gives the add-in its part number. The add-in uses that to find the component in the open design, then reads that component's item number from the Data Model. Fusion Manage is never searched by it.

Map Item Number to the Fusion Manage field that holds it: see The item number. See also End-to-End Workflow.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
Properties are read for each component, up to 500 per component.

  • Base properties ship with the Data Model, for example name, description, part number and material.
  • Custom properties come from property collections that an administrator has linked to your hub. The properties offered when you map fields are the ones defined for your hub and applicable to components. Hidden and archived properties are not offered.

To change what is published, change the property on the component in Fusion, save, and publish again. The Data Model is where the value lives, and the add-in only carries it.

docs.title: Physical properties
docs.text:
Physical properties are not stored like ordinary properties. The Data Model calculates them from the geometry, and they are only available once that calculation has completed. The add-in reads them only if a mapping uses them, because they cost an extra request.

  • A component whose physical properties are not ready yet simply has none to publish. The rest of its properties still publish.
  • The Data Model gives lengths, areas and volumes in centimetres and mass in kilograms. Each value is converted to the unit the Fusion Manage field is set to (see Physical properties and units). If the field states no unit, the value is sent as the Data Model gave it.
  • Values are sent as plain numbers, without units, since a Fusion Manage number field refuses units.

docs.title: Thumbnails
docs.text: A thumbnail is an image that Fusion generates for each component. The address the Data Model gives for it is short-lived, so the add-in asks for a fresh one at the moment it publishes the item. A component whose thumbnail has not been generated yet is published without an image, and the run records that.

docs.title: Which design is read
docs.text: The add-in reads the design that is open in Fusion, in the Autodesk hub you are working in. For a drawing it follows the drawing's reference to the design it shows. Each component's data is read from the saved version of that design.

docs.title: Before you publish
docs.text:
• The design is saved to the cloud.
  • Fusion has finished processing it.
  • Every component that should become an item has an item number.
  • The properties you plan to map are filled in on the components.
  • If you map physical properties, they have finished calculating.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Tell the add-in which Fusion Manage workspace to write to and which property fills which field: Configuration.

docs.title: Troubleshooting and Limitations
docs.text:
What you'll do here: find the cause of an error message and the fix. Find your message in the table for the area you were using.

I was… Go to Signing in or connecting Sign-in problems Looking at a greyed-out button Buttons are greyed out Publishing Publishing Uploading a STEP file or PDF Upload Using the Item panel Item panel Looking for logs or settings files (for support) Where files are kept Wondering whether something is supported Limitations

docs.title: Sign-in problems
docs.text: Message Cause and fix Client ID is required. / Callback port must be between 1024 and 65535. / At least one scope is required. Complete the Connection tab and save. Tenant is required: use Find in Preferences ▸ Connection, or enter it. Sign in, open a design linked to a Fusion Manage item, click Find next to Tenant, then Save. Or type the part before .autodeskplm360.net. The open design is not linked to a Fusion Manage item. Find reads the tenant from the item the open design is linked to. Open a linked design, or type the tenant. Tenant must be a single name such as mycompany, not an address. Enter only the part before .autodeskplm360.net: letters, digits and hyphens. Insufficient permissions to view the Items workspace with no user mapped to the given client in the log The tenant is wrong, so the request went to another Fusion Manage tenant. Set the correct Tenant in Preferences. Callback port 8765 is unavailable: … Another program is using the port. Choose a different Callback port, register the new callback URL on your APS application, and sign in again. Sign-in timed out. No redirect arrived within 180 seconds. Sign in again and complete the browser step promptly. Sign-in cancelled. You clicked Cancel. Sign-in already in progress. Wait for the current attempt to end or cancel it. The browser shows an error from Autodesk instead of signing in The callback URL or Client ID does not match your APS application. The callback URL must be registered exactly as shown on the Connection tab. Not signed in. / Session expired; sign in again. The stored tokens are gone or can no longer be refreshed. Sign in again.

docs.title: Buttons are greyed out
docs.text:
Hover over the button: the tooltip ends with Not available: and the reason.

  • Messages such as The Items workspace ID is not set. mean no Items workspace has been chosen yet, or its settings are incomplete. Choose the workspace and fix the mappings on the Item Workspace tab (Item Workspace).
  • For the drawing PDF, The drawing has no references yet., … none of the designs is loaded yet. and The top-level component of … has no part number. mean the drawing is not ready. Wait for it to finish loading, or give the top-level component a part number. The add-in rechecks every couple of seconds.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text: Message Cause and fix Insufficient permissions to publish to the Items workspace. Missing: … Your Fusion Manage user lacks the named permissions. Ask your administrator. Publishing needs View Items, Add Items, Edit Items, View BOM, Add To BOM and Edit BOM. Could not check your permissions in Fusion Manage: … The permissions request failed for a reason other than being refused: check the active hub, your network and sign-in. Set the Items workspace ID in Settings first. No Items workspace is chosen yet. Choose it from the Workspace drop-down on the Item Workspace tab. Could not find the Data Model id of the open design. The design is not saved to the cloud, or its Data Model reference is not available yet. Save the design and try again. n Fusion Manage items carry the item number … Renumber or remove the extra items. (status Shared number) More than one Fusion Manage item has this item number. Renumber or remove the extra items in Fusion Manage, then refresh. A publish that meets such a number fails before it writes anything. No value in the Data Model, not sent: … A mapped property is empty in the Data Model, so the field is left alone. Fill the property in Fusion if you want it published. '…' is not an option of … in Fusion Manage, so it was not sent. The target field is a picklist and the value matches none of its options. Add the option in Fusion Manage or correct the value. Make sure both picklists have the same values (see Picklists). The rest of the item is still sent. A row is missing after Add default fields The workspace has no field with that field ID, and defaults for missing fields are skipped without a warning. Add the field in Fusion Manage with the exact ID (see Default fields), validate the workspace, and load the defaults again. No thumbnail (The Data Model has no thumbnail for this component yet.) The thumbnail has not been generated yet. Open the design and let Fusion finish processing, then publish again. A "component link" step failed No component was found for the item. Check the component-linking field and that the component exists in the picklist. The item itself is still published. Some items failed and others did not Open the Job Queue for the reason of each row. Fix the cause, then use Retry on that job: what Fusion Manage already accepted is skipped. A request fails with 429, 502, 503 or 504 Reads are retried up to three times. If it persists, wait and send the folder again.

docs.title: Upload
docs.text: Message Cause and fix No item exists for … Publish the item first, or check the part number. Open the design to publish as a STEP file first. Open a design. No component with part number … in the open design. The selected component has no part number, or it is not in the open design. Fusion could not export the STEP file. Fusion refused the export. The message lists what was tried: occurrence, component and own document. A component nested inside another may have no document of its own. Fusion reported the PDF as exported, but no file was written. The drawing had not finished loading. Wait and try again. A file is already being uploaded. Only one upload runs at a time.

docs.title: Item panel
docs.text:
• No item exists for …: the part number has no item. Check it, or publish.
  • Insufficient permissions to view the Items workspace.: you lack View Items.
  • A tab is disabled or missing: your user or workspace does not provide it.

docs.title: Where files are kept
docs.text:
What Windows macOS Configuration (config.json) %APPDATA%\MfgToFm ~/Library/Application Support/MfgToFm Sign-in tokens Encrypted file under %LOCALAPPDATA%\MfgToFm Login Keychain Logs %LOCALAPPDATA%\MfgToFm\logs ~/Library/Logs/MfgToFm/logs Publish runs and upload files (MfgToFm) %TEMP%\MfgToFm $TMPDIR/MfgToFm

A run that goes through has its folder removed when it ends, and Clear finished removes the folders of failed or cancelled runs. Uploads write their STEP or PDF to a folder of their own in the same place and remove it when done. Only folders inside MfgToFm are ever removed.

docs.title: Verbose logging
docs.text:
For support, you can turn on verbose logging by setting the environment variable MFGTOFM_DEBUG=1, or by creating an empty file named debug.flag in the logs folder. Restart the add-in after changing it.

Verbose logs may contain business data

Verbose logs include full request and response bodies, which may contain business data. Review them before sharing. Tokens are never written to logs.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• One workspace. Only the Items workspace is supported. BOMs are those of items; other workspaces are not yet handled.
  • Shared Configuration reads a file from a path, not a web address. The path must be reachable from each machine (on a Mac, a mounted share). Give it as a full path, such as C:\Share\config.json or \\server\share\config.json: ~ and %VARIABLES% are not expanded.
  • Matching is by item number only, taken from the component's Item Number. Components with no item number cannot be published or opened.
  • A drawing is not published. Publishing starts from a design. A drawing can only have its PDF attached to the item of its design's top-level component.
  • STEP uploads one component at a time, and the selection decides which. Large assemblies can take a while to find and export.
  • Releasing is done in Fusion Manage. The Item panel is read-only apart from file uploads.
  • Extra Fusion Manage BOM lines are never removed automatically. You must choose Remove.
  • Items are not deleted by the add-in.
  • Opening a run's folder from the Job Queue uses Windows Explorer.
  • Fusion must be running to create the STEP and PDF files; a publish itself runs in the background and does not need the design to stay open.
